433.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not enter the places of these punished people except weeping. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you.”
433.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in places of collapse and punishment.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet warned against entering the places of the punished except weeping, lest what befell them befall one.

434.matn: Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: ʿAbda informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: “that Umm Salama mentioned to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a church she had seen in the land of Abyssinia, called Māriya. She mentioned to him the pictures she had seen in it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Those are people who, when the righteous servant — or: the righteous man — died among them, built a mosque over his grave and made those pictures in it. Those are the worst of creation in the sight of Allah.”
434.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in a church.” ʿĀʾisha reports that Umm Salama told the Prophet about a church in Abyssinia called Māriya and its pictures; he said that those people had built a mosque over the grave of their righteous servant and put the pictures in it, and called them the worst of creation in the sight of Allah. “Servant” or “man” is a transmitter’s uncertainty about the wording.

435.matn: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī: ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba informed me: that ʿĀʾisha and ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās said: “When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was dying, he began to throw a cloak of his over his face; when he felt distressed under it, he uncovered his face. And while he was like that he said: The curse of Allah be upon the Jews and the Christians: they took the graves of their prophets as mosques.” He was warning against what they had done.
435.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith in a chapter that the source calls only “Chapter,” without a heading. ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbās report that in his final illness the Prophet kept putting a cloak over his face and uncovering it, and said that Allah’s curse is upon the Jews and the Christians who made the graves of their prophets into mosques; the text adds that he was warning against what they had done.

437.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra: that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “May Allah fight the Jews: they took the graves of their prophets as mosques.”
437.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter without a heading. Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet the saying that Allah fight the Jews because they made the graves of their prophets into mosques.

438.matn: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Sayyār — that is Abū al-Ḥakam — narrated to us, he said: Yazīd al-Faqīr narrated to us, he said: Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given five things that none of the prophets before me was given: I was supported with terror at the distance of a month’s journey; the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification; whichever man of my community the time of prayer overtakes, let him pray; spoils of war were made lawful for me; every prophet used to be sent only to his own people, while I was sent to all people; and I was given intercession.”
438.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on the Prophet’s saying that the earth was made for him a place of prayer and a means of purification. Jābir reports five things given to the Prophet and to no prophet before him: support through terror at a month’s distance, the earth as a place of prayer and purification, the lawful spoils, the mission to all people instead of only his own people, and intercession. It also says that anyone from his community should pray wherever the time of prayer overtakes him.

439.matn: ʿUbayd ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: “that a black slave girl belonged to an Arab clan; they freed her, and she stayed with them. She said: A girl of theirs went out wearing a red sash of leather strips. She said: She put it down — or it fell from her —; a kite passed by while it was lying there, took it for meat and snatched it. She said: They looked for it and did not find it. She said: So they suspected me of it. She said: They began to search me, until they even searched her private parts. She said: By Allah, I was standing with them when the kite passed by and dropped it; it fell among them. She said: I said: This is what you suspected me of — you claimed it while I was innocent of it — and here it is! She said: Then she came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and accepted Islam. ʿĀʾisha said: She had a tent in the mosque or a small room. She said: She would come to me and talk with me. She said: She never sat with me without saying: The day of the sash is among the wonders of our Lord — yet truly, He saved me from the land of disbelief. ʿĀʾisha said: I said to her: What is the matter with you, that you never sit with me without saying this? She said: Then she told me this story.”
439.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A woman sleeping in the mosque.” ʿĀʾisha tells of a freed black slave girl who was suspected, and searched, for having taken a red leather sash until a kite dropped it. She came to the Prophet, accepted Islam and afterwards had a tent or small room in the mosque; with ʿĀʾisha she recited a verse about the day of the sash every time and finally told the story.

440.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbaydallāh, he said: Nāfiʿ narrated to me, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed me: “that he used to sleep in the mosque of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was a young unmarried man without a family.”
440.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Men sleeping in the mosque.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that he slept in the Prophet’s mosque as a young unmarried man without a family.

441.matn: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Ḥāzim narrated to us, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Sahl ibn Saʿd, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to the house of Fāṭima and did not find ʿAlī in the house. He said: Where is your cousin? She said: Something happened between him and me, and he was angry with me, went out and did not take his midday rest with me. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to a person: Look where he is. He came and said: O Messenger of Allah, he is in the mosque, sleeping. The Messenger of Allah came, and he was lying on his side, his cloak had slipped off his side, and dust had gotten on him. The Messenger of Allah began to wipe it off him and said: Get up, Abū Turāb, get up, Abū Turāb.”
441.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Sahl reports that the Prophet did not find ʿAlī at Fāṭima’s house because he had gone out after a quarrel, and found him sleeping in the mosque, his cloak slipped and covered in dust; the Prophet wiped the dust off him and called him “Abū Turāb.”

442.matn: Yūsuf ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayra, he said: “I saw seventy of the People of the Ṣuffa; none of them had a cloak, only either a waist-wrapper or a sheet, tied around their necks. Some reached halfway down the shins, some reached the ankles, and he would hold it together with his hand, disliking that his private parts be seen.”
442.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter. Abū Hurayra reports that he saw seventy of the People of the Ṣuffa who had no cloak, only a waist-wrapper or a sheet tied around the neck that reached down to varying lengths; the wearer held it together with his hand so that his private parts would not be seen.

443.matn: Khallād ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Misʿar narrated to us, he said: Muḥārib ibn Dithār narrated to us, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh, he said: “I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque — Misʿar said: I think he said: in the forenoon. He said: Pray two rakʿas. And he owed me a debt; so he repaid me and gave me more.”
443.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Prayer on returning from a journey.” Jābir reports that he came to the Prophet in the mosque; the narrator Misʿar is unsure whether it was in the forenoon. The Prophet told him to pray two rakʿas and repaid the debt he owed him with an addition.

444.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn az-Zubayr, from ʿAmr ibn Sulaym az-Zuraqī, from Abū Qatāda as-Sulamī: “that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rakʿas before he sits.”
444.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Prayer on returning from a journey.” Abū Qatāda reports from the Prophet that whoever enters the mosque should pray two rakʿas before sitting down.

445.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Abū az-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra: “that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: The angels pray for one of you as long as he remains in his place of prayer where he prayed, as long as he has not broken his ablution. They say: O Allah, forgive him! O Allah, have mercy on him!”
445.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Breaking ablution in the mosque.” Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that the angels ask for blessing upon the worshipper as long as he stays in his place of prayer and has not broken his ablution; they say: “O Allah, forgive him, O Allah, have mercy on him.”

446.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, he said: Nāfiʿ narrated to us: that ʿAbdallāh informed him: “that the mosque in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was built of mud bricks, its roof of palm fronds, and its pillars of palm trunks. Abū Bakr added nothing to it, but ʿUmar added to it: he built it on its original structure from the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with mud bricks and palm fronds, and restored its pillars in wood. Then ʿUthmān altered it and added a great deal to it: he built its wall of carved stones and lime plaster (al-qaṣṣa), made its pillars of carved stones, and its roof of teak.”
446.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The building of the mosque.” Ibn ʿUmar describes the Prophet’s mosque as built of mud bricks, with a roof of palm fronds and pillars of palm trunks. Abū Bakr added nothing; ʿUmar rebuilt it in the same manner and replaced the pillars with wood; ʿUthmān enlarged it greatly and used carved stones, lime plaster and teak.

447.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Mukhtār narrated to us, he said: Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated to us, from ʿIkrima: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me and to his son ʿAlī: “Go to Abū Saʿīd and listen to his narration. So we went, and he was in a garden, repairing it. He took his cloak and sat wrapped in it, then began to narrate to us until he came to the mention of the building of the mosque. He said: We used to carry one brick at a time, while ʿAmmār carried two bricks at a time. The Prophet saw him, wiped the dust off him and said: Alas, ʿAmmār! [The rebellious group will kill him.] He calls them to Paradise, and they call him to the Fire.” He said: ʿAmmār says: I seek refuge in Allah from trials.
447.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Cooperation in building the mosque.” Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī recounts that while building the mosque each carried one brick, but ʿAmmār two, and how the Prophet wiped the dust off him. The sentence in square brackets stands marked as such in the Arabic text; ʿAmmār sought refuge from trials.

448.matn: Qutayba narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Sahl, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent word to a woman: Order your slave, the carpenter, to make me some wooden steps on which I may sit.”
448.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Seeking help from the carpenter and craftsmen for the pulpit’s wood and the mosque.” Sahl reports that the Prophet sent word to a woman to instruct her slave, the carpenter, to make him wooden steps to sit on.

449.matn: Khallād narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ayman narrated to us, from his father, from Jābir: “that a woman said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I not make you something to sit on? For I have a slave who is a carpenter. He said: If you wish. So she had the pulpit made.”
449.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Seeking help from the carpenter and craftsmen for the pulpit’s wood and the mosque.” Jābir reports that a woman offered to have her carpenter slave make the Prophet something to sit on; he agreed, and so the pulpit was made.

450.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to me, he said: ʿAmr informed me that Bukayr narrated to him that ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatāda narrated to him that he heard ʿUbaydallāh al-Khawlānī: “that he heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān say, when people were speaking about him for building the mosque of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: You have said too much, and I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever builds a mosque — Bukayr said: I think he said: seeking thereby the face of Allah — Allah will build for him the like of it in Paradise.”
450.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who builds a mosque.” ʿUthmān answers the people’s talk about his building of the Prophet’s mosque with the hadith that Allah builds for whoever builds a mosque the like of it in Paradise. The narrator Bukayr is unsure whether the addition “seeking the face of Allah” was said.

451.matn: Qutayba ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: I said to ʿAmr: Did you hear Jābir ibn ʿAbdallāh say: “A man passed through the mosque with arrows, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Hold them by their heads.”
451.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Holding the arrowheads when passing through the mosque.” The narrator asks ʿAmr whether he heard Jābir say: A man passed through the mosque with arrows, and the Prophet told him to hold them by the heads.

452.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, he said: Abū Burda ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Burda, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever passes through any of our mosques or our markets with arrows, let him hold them by their heads, lest he wound a Muslim with his palm.”
452.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Passing through the mosque.” The Prophet instructs that whoever passes through mosques or markets with arrows should hold them by the heads, so that he does not hurt a Muslim with his hand.

453.matn: Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from az-Zuhrī, he said: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed me: “that he heard Ḥassān ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī calling Abū Hurayra to witness: I adjure you by Allah, did you hear the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: O Ḥassān, answer on behalf of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit (Rūḥ al-Qudus)! Abū Hurayra said: Yes.”
453.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Poetry in the mosque.” Ḥassān ibn Thābit calls Abū Hurayra to witness before Allah as to whether he heard the Prophet say: “O Ḥassān, answer on behalf of the Messenger of Allah; O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit.” Abū Hurayra confirms with “Yes.”

454.matn: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: ʿUrwa ibn az-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾisha said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one day at the door of my chamber, while the Abyssinians were playing in the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was screening me with his cloak; I was watching their play.”
454.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The spearmen in the mosque.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she saw the Prophet at the door of her chamber while the Abyssinians were playing in the mosque; he screened her with his cloak, and she watched their play.

455.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir added: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while the Abyssinians were playing with their spears.”
455.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The spearmen in the mosque.” It is an addition by Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir with its own chain to ʿĀʾisha, and reports in shorter form that she saw the Prophet while the Abyssinians were playing with their spears.

456.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from ʿAmra, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “Barīra came to her asking her for help regarding her contract of manumission. She said: If you wish, I will pay your people (the amount), and the walāʾ (the right of patronage) will be mine. And her people said: If you wish, give her what remains — and Sufyān once said: If you wish, buy her freedom, and the walāʾ will be ours. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, I mentioned that to him. He said: Buy her and free her, for the walāʾ belongs to the one who frees. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up on the pulpit — and Sufyān once said: So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit — and said: What is the matter with people who stipulate conditions that are not in the Book of Allah? Whoever stipulates a condition that is not in the Book of Allah, it is not his, even if he stipulates it a hundred times.” ʿAlī said: Yaḥyā and ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: from Yaḥyā, from ʿAmra; and Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn said, from Yaḥyā, he said: I heard ʿAmra say: I heard ʿĀʾisha. Mālik narrated it from Yaḥyā, from ʿAmra: that Barīra — and he did not mention: “he ascended the pulpit.”
456.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Mentioning buying and selling on the pulpit in the mosque.” ʿĀʾisha tells of Barīra’s contract of manumission: the Prophet says the walāʾ belongs to the one who frees, and then speaks from the pulpit against conditions that are not in the Book of Allah. The text notes variations in Sufyān’s wording and different chains; Mālik narrates the episode without mentioning the pulpit.

457.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Yūnus informed us, from az-Zuhrī, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from Kaʿb: “that he demanded repayment from Ibn Abī Ḥadrad of a debt he had against him, in the mosque; their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard them while in his house. He came out to them until he lifted the curtain of his chamber and called: O Kaʿb! He said: At your service, O Messenger of Allah! He said: Remit this part of your debt. And he gestured to him: that is, the half. He said: I have done so, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Get up and pay him.”
457.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Demanding repayment and pressing a debtor in the mosque.” Kaʿb reports that he demanded a debt from Ibn Abī Ḥadrad in the mosque; their voices rose, and the Prophet came out and asked Kaʿb to remit half, which he did. Then the Prophet told the debtor to pay the rest.

458.matn: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thābit, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayra: “that a black man or a black woman used to sweep the mosque and died. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked about him, and they said: He has died. He said: Why did you not inform me? Show me his grave — or he said: her grave. So he came to the grave and prayed over her.”
458.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Sweeping the mosque and picking up rags, dirt and twigs.” Abū Hurayra reports about a black man or woman who used to sweep the mosque and died. The Prophet asked about the person, asked to be shown the grave, and prayed there over her. Whether it was a man or a woman is not clear in the text.

459.matn: ʿAbdān narrated to us, from Abū Ḥamza, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “When the verses of Sūrat al-Baqara concerning usury were revealed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the mosque and recited them to the people; then he prohibited the trade in wine.”
459.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The prohibition of trade in wine, announced in the mosque.” ʿĀʾisha reports that after the verses of Sūrat al-Baqara on usury were revealed, the Prophet went out to the mosque, recited them to the people, and then prohibited the trade in wine.

460.matn: Aḥmad ibn Wāqid narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Thābit, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayra: “that a woman or a man used to sweep the mosque — and I think it was only a woman —; then he mentioned the hadith of the Prophet: that he prayed at her grave.”
460.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Servants for the mosque.” Abū Hurayra reports about a woman or a man who used to sweep the mosque; the narrator inclines to “woman.” He refers to the report that the Prophet prayed at this person’s grave.

461.matn: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Rawḥ and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us, from Shuʿba, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “An ʿifrīt from among the jinn lunged at me last night — or he said a similar word — to interrupt my prayer. Allah gave me power over him, and I wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque so that by morning all of you could look at him. Then I remembered the saying of my brother Sulaymān: ‘My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me.’” Rawḥ said: “So he sent him back humiliated.”
461.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The captive or debtor tied up in the mosque.” Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that an ʿifrīt from among the jinn lunged at him in the night to interrupt his prayer, and Allah gave him power over him. He wanted to tie him to a pillar, but remembered Sulaymān’s supplication and sent him back humiliated, as Rawḥ adds.

462.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd narrated to us that he heard Abū Hurayra say: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent cavalry toward Najd; they brought a man from Banū Ḥanīfa called Thumāma ibn Uthāl, and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to him and said: Release Thumāma. So he went to palm trees near the mosque, bathed, then entered the mosque and said: I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.”
462.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bathing on embracing Islam, and tying the captive in the mosque.” Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet’s cavalry brought Thumāma ibn Uthāl of Banū Ḥanīfa and tied him to a pillar of the mosque. At the Prophet’s order he was released, bathed at the palm trees near the mosque, and pronounced the declaration of faith in the mosque.

463.matn: Zakariyyāʾ ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “Saʿd was struck on the day of the Trench in the arm vein (al-akḥal). So the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pitched a tent in the mosque so that he could visit him from nearby. And it startled them — in the mosque there was a tent of Banū Ghifār — only that blood was flowing toward them. They said: O people of the tent, what is this that is coming to us from your side? And it was Saʿd, his wound streaming blood, and he died in it.”
463.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A tent in the mosque for the sick and others.” ʿĀʾisha reports that Saʿd was struck in the arm vein on the day of the Trench and the Prophet pitched a tent for him in the mosque to visit him from nearby. When blood flowed toward the tent of Banū Ghifār, it turned out to come from Saʿd’s wound; he died in the tent. The text mentions only “Saʿd.”

464.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal, from ʿUrwa, from Zaynab bint Abī Salama, from Umm Salama, she said: “I complained to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that I was ailing. He said: Circumambulate behind the people while you are riding. So I circumambulated while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying beside the House, reciting aṭ-Ṭūr: ‘And by a written Book.’”
464.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bringing a camel into the mosque for a reason.” Umm Salama reports that she complained to the Prophet of her illness; he had her perform the ṭawāf riding behind the people, while he prayed beside the House reciting Sūrat aṭ-Ṭūr.

465.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, he said: Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from Qatāda, he said: Anas narrated to us: “that two men from the Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, left the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a dark night, and with them were what seemed like two lamps shining before them. When they parted, each of them had one with him until he reached his family.”
465.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Bringing a camel into the mosque for a reason.” Anas reports that two Companions left the Prophet on a dark night and two lamp-like lights shone before them; when they parted, one stayed with each until he reached his family.

466.matn: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to us, he said: Fulayḥ narrated to us, he said: Abū an-Naḍr narrated to us, from ʿUbayd ibn Ḥunayn, from Busr ibn Saʿīd, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave a sermon and said: Allah gave a servant the choice between this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Allah. Abū Bakr wept, may Allah be pleased with him. I said to myself: Why is this old man weeping? If Allah gave a servant the choice between this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Allah — the servant was the Messenger of Allah, and Abū Bakr was the most knowledgeable among us. He said: O Abū Bakr, do not weep! The most generous of people to me in companionship and wealth is Abū Bakr. And if I were to take an intimate friend (khalīl) from my community, I would take Abū Bakr; but there is the brotherhood of Islam and its affection. No door in the mosque shall remain that is not closed, except the door of Abū Bakr.”
466.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The small door and passage in the mosque.” Abū Saʿīd reports a sermon of the Prophet about a servant who was given the choice between the world and what is with Allah; Abū Bakr wept, and Abū Saʿīd realized that the Prophet himself was meant. The Prophet acknowledged Abū Bakr’s companionship and wealth and ordered that all doors to the mosque be closed except Abū Bakr’s.

467.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad al-Juʿfī narrated to us, he said: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: I heard Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out during his illness in which he died, with his head bound with a cloth, sat on the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, and then said: There is no one among people who has been more generous to me in himself and his wealth than Abū Bakr ibn Abī Quḥāfa. And if I were to take an intimate friend (khalīl) from among people, I would take Abū Bakr as an intimate friend; but the friendship of Islam is more excellent. Close for me every small door (khawkha) in this mosque except the door of Abū Bakr.”
467.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The small door and passage in the mosque.” Ibn ʿAbbās reports that during his last illness the Prophet ascended the pulpit with his head bound, praised Allah, and highlighted Abū Bakr’s generosity with himself and his wealth. He ordered that all small doors to the mosque be closed except Abū Bakr’s.

468.matn: Abū an-Nuʿmān and Qutayba narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to Mecca and called ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa, who opened the door; the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Bilāl, Usāma ibn Zayd and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa entered, and then the door was closed. He stayed in it for a while, then they came out. Ibn ʿUmar said: I hurried and asked Bilāl. He said: He prayed in it. I said: In which spot? He said: Between the two pillars. Ibn ʿUmar said: I forgot to ask him how much he prayed.”
468.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Doors and locks for the Kaʿba and mosques.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that in Mecca the Prophet entered the Kaʿba with Bilāl, Usāma ibn Zayd and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa, and the door was closed. According to Bilāl, he prayed in it between the two pillars; Ibn ʿUmar forgot to ask how much he prayed.

469.matn: Qutayba narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd, that he heard Abū Hurayra say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent cavalry toward Najd; they brought a man from Banū Ḥanīfa called Thumāma ibn Uthāl, and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque.”
469.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “An idolater entering the mosque.” Abū Hurayra reports in the short version that the cavalry sent by the Prophet brought Thumāma ibn Uthāl of Banū Ḥanīfa and tied him to a pillar of the mosque.

470.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: al-Juʿayd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Khuṣayfa narrated to me, from as-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, he said: “I was standing in the mosque when a man threw a pebble at me. I looked, and it was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He said: Go and bring me these two. I brought them to him. He said: Who are you two, or where are you from? They said: From the people of aṭ-Ṭāʾif. He said: If you were from the people of this town, I would have punished you painfully — you raise your voices in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
470.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Raising the voice in mosques.” As-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd reports that ʿUmar got his attention with a pebble and had two men from aṭ-Ṭāʾif brought who had raised their voices in the mosque. ʿUmar said he would have punished them painfully had they been from the town.

471.matn: Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Yūnus ibn Yazīd informed me, from Ibn Shihāb: ʿAbdallāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik narrated to me that Kaʿb ibn Mālik informed him: “that in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he demanded from Ibn Abī Ḥadrad, in the mosque, a debt owed to him; their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard them in his house. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to them until he lifted the curtain of his chamber and called: O Kaʿb ibn Mālik! O Kaʿb! He said: At your service, O Messenger of Allah! So he gestured with his hand that he should remit half of his debt. Kaʿb said: I have done so, O Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Get up and pay him.”
471.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Raising the voice in mosques.” Kaʿb ibn Mālik reports that when he demanded a debt from Ibn Abī Ḥadrad in the mosque, their voices rose; the Prophet came out, gestured to remit half, and then told the debtor to pay the rest.

472.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, from ʿUbaydallāh, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: “A man asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit: What do you say about the night prayer? He said: Two by two; and if one fears the morning, he prays one, and it makes what he has prayed odd (witr).” And he used to say: “Make witr the last of your prayer, for the Prophet commanded it.”
472.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Circles and sitting in the mosque.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that when asked about the night prayer, the Prophet answered from the pulpit: two by two, and if the morning is feared, one rakʿa as witr. Ibn ʿUmar adds that one should make witr the conclusion of the prayer.

473.matn: Abū an-Nuʿmān narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: “that a man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was giving a sermon, and said: How is the night prayer? He said: Two by two; and if you fear the morning, pray witr with one; it makes odd what you have prayed.” Al-Walīd ibn Kathīr said: ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to me: Ibn ʿUmar narrated to them: that a man called out to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque.
473.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Circles and sitting in the mosque.” Ibn ʿUmar relates the Prophet’s answer to the question about the night prayer: two by two, and if the morning is feared, one as witr. The addition of al-Walīd ibn Kathīr with its own chain states that the man called out to the Prophet in the mosque.

474.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥa: that Abū Murra, the freedman of ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib, informed him, from Abū Wāqid al-Laythī, he said: “While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in the mosque, three men came; two approached the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one went away. One of the two saw a gap and sat down; the other sat behind them. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, he said: Shall I not tell you about the three? As for one of them, he took refuge with Allah, so Allah gave him refuge; as for the other, he was shy, so Allah was shy of him; and as for the other, he turned away, so Allah turned away from him.”
474.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Circles and sitting in the mosque.” Abū Wāqid reports three men who came to the Prophet’s gathering in the mosque: one sat in a gap, one behind the others, and one went away. The Prophet explained that Allah gave the first refuge, was shy of the second, and turned away from the third.

475.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from his paternal uncle, that he “saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lying on his back in the mosque, with one leg placed on the other.” And from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: ʿUmar and ʿUthmān used to do that.
475.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Lying on one’s back in the mosque and stretching the leg.” ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm reports from his uncle that he saw the Prophet lying on his back in the mosque with one leg over the other. The second part, via Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, is a statement about the practice of ʿUmar and ʿUthmān and not a saying of the Prophet.

476.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: ʿUrwa ibn az-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Ever since I have known my parents, they followed the religion (dīn), and no day passed over us without the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, coming to us at both ends of the day, morning and evening. Then it occurred to Abū Bakr, and he built a place of prayer (masjid) in the courtyard of his house; he used to pray in it and recite the Qurʾān. The wives of the polytheists and their children would stand by him, marveling at him and looking at him. Abū Bakr was a man who wept much; he could not control his eyes when he recited the Qurʾān. This alarmed the nobles of Quraysh among the polytheists.”
476.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A mosque on the road without harm to people.” ʿĀʾisha reports that Abū Bakr built a place of prayer in the courtyard of his house, where he prayed and recited the Qurʾān; the polytheists’ women and children watched him, and he wept much during recitation, which alarmed the nobles of Quraysh.

477.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The prayer in congregation exceeds his prayer in his house and his prayer in his market by twenty-five degrees. For when one of you performs ablution and does it well, and comes to the mosque desiring nothing but prayer, he takes no step without Allah raising him a degree by it and removing a sin from him, until he enters the mosque. And when he enters the mosque, he is in prayer as long as the prayer detains him; and the angels pray — that is, for him — as long as he is in his place where he prays: O Allah, forgive him, O Allah, have mercy on him, as long as he does not break his ablution in it.”
477.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying in the market mosque.” Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that prayer in congregation exceeds prayer at home and in the market by twenty-five degrees, that each step to the mosque raises a degree and removes a sin, and that the angels ask for blessing upon the one sitting as long as he does not break his ablution.

478.matn: Ḥāmid ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Bishr, he said: ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: Wāqid narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿUmar or Ibn ʿAmr: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, interlaced his fingers.”
478.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Interlacing the fingers in the mosque and elsewhere.” The text briefly reports that the Prophet interlaced his fingers. The narrator is unsure whether the Companion was Ibn ʿUmar or Ibn ʿAmr.

480.matn: And ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī said: ʿĀṣim ibn Muḥammad narrated to us: I heard this hadith from my father but did not retain it; then Wāqid corrected it for me, from his father, he said: I heard my father say: ʿAbdallāh said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “O ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr, how will you be when you remain among the dregs of people?” — with this (wording).
480.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “Interlacing the fingers in the mosque and elsewhere.” It is introduced with “and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAlī said” and is given only as a fragment: the Prophet asks ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr how he will be when he remains among the dregs of people. The rest of the wording is not given in the text.

481.matn: Khallād ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Burda ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Burda, from his grandfather, from Abū Mūsā, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The believer to the believer is like a building, parts of which support other parts.” And he interlaced his fingers.
481.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Interlacing the fingers in the mosque and elsewhere.” Abū Mūsā relates the Prophet’s parable that the believer to the believer is like a building whose parts support one another; the Prophet interlaced his fingers as he said it.

482.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Shumayl narrated to us: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in one of the two evening prayers — Ibn Sīrīn said: Abū Hurayra named it, but I forgot — he said: He prayed two rakʿas with us, then gave the salām, went to a piece of wood laid across in the mosque, leaned on it as if angry, placed his right hand on the left, interlaced his fingers, and placed his right cheek on the back of his left hand. The hasty ones went out through the doors of the mosque, saying: Has the prayer been shortened? Among the people were Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, but they were afraid to speak to him. Among the people was a man with long hands, called Dhū l-Yadayn. He said: O Messenger of Allah, did you forget, or has the prayer been shortened? He said: I did not forget, and it has not been shortened. Then he said: Is it as Dhū l-Yadayn says? They said: Yes. So he stepped forward and prayed what he had left, then gave the salām, then said the takbīr and prostrated like his prostration or longer, then raised his head and said the takbīr, then said the takbīr and prostrated like his prostration or longer, then raised his head and said the takbīr.” They would sometimes ask him: “And then he gave the salām?” He would say: “I was told that ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: Then he gave the salām.”
482.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Interlacing the fingers in the mosque and elsewhere.” Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet gave the salām after two rakʿas, leaned on a piece of wood and interlaced his fingers; Dhū l-Yadayn asked whether he had forgotten or the prayer had been shortened. After those present confirmed, the Prophet prayed what was left out and prostrated twice. The closing remark about the salām is Ibn Sīrīn’s statement that he was told this by ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn.

483.matn: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to us, he said: Fuḍayl ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: Mūsā ibn ʿUqba narrated to us, he said: “I saw Sālim ibn ʿAbdallāh seeking out certain places along the road and praying in them; he related that his father used to pray in them and that he had seen the Prophet ﷺ praying in those places. And Nāfiʿ related to me from Ibn ʿUmar that he used to pray in those places. I asked Sālim, and I know only that he agreed with Nāfiʿ in all the places, except that the two differed regarding a mosque at Sharaf al-Rawḥāʾ.”
483.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” Mūsā ibn ʿUqba reports that Sālim ibn ʿAbdallāh sought out certain places along the road to pray there, because his father prayed there and had seen the Prophet praying there; Nāfiʿ reports the same from Ibn ʿUmar. According to Mūsā, the two agreed except about one mosque at Sharaf al-Rawḥāʾ.

484.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, he said: Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to us, he said: Mūsā ibn ʿUqba narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ: ʿAbdallāh informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ “used to alight at Dhū l-Ḥulayfa when he performed ʿumra, and on his pilgrimage when he performed ḥajj, beneath a samura tree at the place of the mosque that is at Dhū l-Ḥulayfa. And when he returned from a campaign — on that road — or from ḥajj or ʿumra, he would descend from the bottom of a wadi, and when he came out of the bottom of the wadi, he made his mount kneel at the Baṭḥāʾ that is on the eastern edge of the wadi, and rested there for the night until morning — not at the mosque built of stones, and not on the hillock on which the mosque stands. There was a channel there beside which ʿAbdallāh prayed; in its bed were sand mounds, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray there. Then the flood spread the Baṭḥāʾ over it until that place where ʿAbdallāh used to pray was buried.”
484.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” Ibn ʿUmar describes where the Prophet alighted at Dhū l-Ḥulayfa beneath a samura tree and where he spent the night at the Baṭḥāʾ on his return. The text also mentions that the flood buried a place where ʿAbdallāh used to pray.

485.matn: And that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar related to him: “The Prophet ﷺ prayed where the small mosque is, which lies before the mosque at Sharaf al-Rawḥāʾ.” ʿAbdallāh knew the place where the Prophet ﷺ had prayed, and he would say: “Then to your right, when you stand in the mosque to pray. That mosque is on the right edge of the road as you go to Mecca; between it and the larger mosque is a stone’s throw or about that.”
485.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” It begins with “and that,” and so continues the preceding narration. Ibn ʿUmar names the small mosque before the mosque at Sharaf al-Rawḥāʾ as a place where the Prophet prayed and describes its position on the right edge of the road toward Mecca.

486.matn: “And that Ibn ʿUmar used to pray toward the ʿIrq that is at the Munṣaraf of al-Rawḥāʾ. The end of the edge of that ʿIrq reaches the edge of the road, before the mosque that lies between it and the Munṣaraf, as you go to Mecca. A mosque had been built there, but ʿAbdallāh did not pray in that mosque; he left it on his left and behind him, and prayed in front of it, toward the ʿIrq itself. And ʿAbdallāh would set out from al-Rawḥāʾ and would not pray the noon prayer until he reached that place, and there he prayed the noon prayer. And when he was coming from Mecca, if he passed it an hour before dawn or at the end of the night, he rested there until he prayed the dawn prayer there.”
486.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” It begins with “and that,” without an introductory chain, and so continues the preceding narrations. It describes where Ibn ʿUmar prayed at the ʿIrq near al-Rawḥāʾ and that he avoided the mosque built there.

487.matn: And that ʿAbdallāh related to him: “The Prophet ﷺ used to alight beneath a huge tree, before al-Ruwaytha, on the right of the road and facing the road, in a flat, level place, until he comes from a hillock that lies two miles before the Barīd of al-Ruwaytha. Its top was broken and bent over in its middle, but it stands on a trunk, and around its trunk are many sand mounds.”
487.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” Ibn ʿUmar describes the Prophet’s resting place beneath a huge tree before al-Ruwaytha. The text consists only of place indications and a description of the tree.

488.matn: And that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar related to him: “The Prophet ﷺ prayed at the edge of a talʿa beyond al-ʿArj, as you go toward a plateau. At that mosque there are two or three graves; on the graves is a pile of stones, on the right of the road, by the salam trees of the road, among those salam trees. ʿAbdallāh used to set out from al-ʿArj after the sun had declined in the midday heat, and would pray the noon prayer in that mosque.”
488.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” It begins with “and that,” and so continues the preceding ones. Ibn ʿUmar names a place where the Prophet prayed beyond al-ʿArj and describes its location; the text contains only place indications.

489.matn: And that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar related to him: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ alighted at some great trees on the left of the road, in a watercourse before Harshā. That watercourse adjoins Kurāʿ Harshā; between it and the road is about a bowshot. And ʿAbdallāh used to pray toward a tree, which is the nearest of those trees to the road and the tallest of them.”
489.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” Ibn ʿUmar describes the Prophet’s resting place at great trees before Harshā and the tree toward which ʿAbdallāh prayed. The text contains only place indications.

490.matn: And that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar related to him: “The Prophet ﷺ used to alight in the watercourse that lies in the nearer part of Marr al-Ẓahrān, before Medina, when he descended from al-Ṣafrāwāt. He alighted in the bed of that watercourse on the left of the road as you go to Mecca; between the Messenger of Allah’s ﷺ resting place and the road there is only a stone’s throw.”
490.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” Ibn ʿUmar describes the Prophet’s resting place in a watercourse at Marr al-Ẓahrān. The text contains only place indications.

491.matn: And that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar related to him: “The Prophet ﷺ used to alight at Dhū Ṭuwā and spend the night there until morning; he would pray the dawn prayer when he arrived in Mecca. That place of prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is on a rough hillock, not in the mosque that was built there, but lower than it, on a rough hillock.”
491.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet alighted at Dhū Ṭuwā, spent the night there and prayed the dawn prayer on arriving in Mecca, and states the location of the place of prayer in relation to the mosque built there.

492.matn: And that ʿAbdallāh related to him: “The Prophet ﷺ faced the two notches of the mountain that lies between him and the long mountain in the direction of the Kaaba; he made the mosque that was built there to the left of the mosque at the edge of the hillock. The Prophet’s ﷺ place of prayer is lower than it, on the black hillock; you leave ten cubits or so of the hillock, then you pray facing the two notches of the mountain that lies between you and the Kaaba.”
492.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the narration under the chapter “The mosques on the roads to Medina and the places where the Prophet ﷺ prayed.” Ibn ʿUmar gives the Prophet’s place of prayer through place indications: facing the two notches of a mountain in the direction of the Kaaba, on the black hillock. The text contains only place indications.

493.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: “I came riding a she-donkey, and I was at that time close to reaching puberty; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer at Minā, not facing a wall. I passed in front of part of the row, dismounted, let the she-donkey graze, and entered the row; and no one objected to that.”
493.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The imam's sutra is the sutra of those behind him.” Ibn ʿAbbās reports that as an adolescent he passed in front of part of the row on a she-donkey while the Prophet was leading the prayer at Minā, and that no one objected.

494.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: ʿUbaydallāh narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ “when he went out on the day of the festival, would order the spear, and it would be set before him; then he would pray toward it with the people behind him. And he would do that on journeys too; from that point the rulers adopted it.”
494.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The imam's sutra is the sutra of those behind him.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that on the festival day the Prophet had a spear set before him and prayed toward it with the people behind him, and that he did the same on journeys. The remark that the rulers adopted it from that point is in the text.

495.matn: Abū l-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfa, he said: I heard my father: The Prophet ﷺ “led them in prayer at al-Baṭḥāʾ with a short spear (ʿanaza) before him: the noon prayer two rakʿas and the afternoon prayer two rakʿas; the woman and the donkey passed in front of him.”
495.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The imam's sutra is the sutra of those behind him.” The narrator reports that at al-Baṭḥāʾ the Prophet led the noon and afternoon prayers, two rakʿas each, with an ʿanaza before him, and that a woman and a donkey passed in front of him.

496.matn: ʿAmr ibn Zurāra narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī Ḥāzim informed us, from his father, from Sahl, he said: “Between the place of prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the wall was the passage of a sheep.”
496.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “How much distance there should be between the one praying and the sutra.” Sahl describes the distance between the Prophet’s place of prayer and the wall as the passage of a sheep. The text gives no exact measurement.

497.matn: Al-Makkī narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Salama, he said: “The wall of the mosque by the minbar — a sheep could hardly pass through it.”
497.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “How much distance there should be between the one praying and the sutra.” Salama describes the narrow space at the wall of the mosque by the minbar, which a sheep could hardly pass through. The text gives no exact measurement.

498.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbaydallāh: Nāfiʿ informed me, from ʿAbdallāh: The Prophet ﷺ “had the spear planted for him and would pray toward it.”
498.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying towards a spear.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that a spear was planted in the ground for the Prophet and he prayed toward it.

499.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfa narrated to us, he said: I heard my father, he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us in the midday heat; water for ablution was brought and he performed ablution. Then he led us in the noon and afternoon prayers, with a short spear (ʿanaza) before him, while the woman and the donkey passed behind it.”
499.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying towards a short spear (ʿanaza).” The narrator reports that after ablution the Prophet led the noon and afternoon prayers with an ʿanaza before him, and that the woman and the donkey passed behind the ʿanaza.

500.matn: Muḥammad ibn Ḥātim ibn Buzayʿ narrated to us, he said: Shādhān narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūna, he said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say: “When the Prophet ﷺ went out for his need, a boy and I would follow him, and we had a walking stick (ʿukkāza) — or a staff or an ʿanaza — and we had a water container (idāwa); and when he had finished his need, we would hand him the water container.”
500.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying towards a short spear (ʿanaza).” Anas reports that he and a boy followed the Prophet when he went out for his need, with a staff or an ʿanaza and a water container. No prayer is mentioned in this text.

501.matn: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū Juḥayfa, he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in the midday heat and prayed at al-Baṭḥāʾ the noon and afternoon prayers, two rakʿas each; he set up an ʿanaza before him and performed ablution, and the people began to wipe themselves with his ablution water.”
501.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The sutra in Mecca and elsewhere.” Abū Juḥayfa reports that the Prophet prayed the noon and afternoon prayers at al-Baṭḥāʾ, two rakʿas each, set up an ʿanaza before him, and that the people wiped themselves with his ablution water.

502.matn: Al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd narrated to us, he said: “I used to come with Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ, and he would pray by the pillar that is by the muṣḥaf. I said: O Abū Muslim, I see you seeking out the prayer at this pillar? He said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ seeking out the prayer there.”
502.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying towards a pillar.” Yazīd reports that Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ prayed by a particular pillar and gave as his reason that he had seen the Prophet deliberately pray there.

503.matn: Qabīṣa narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir, from Anas, he said: “I saw the senior Companions of the Prophet ﷺ hurrying to the pillars at the Maghrib prayer.” And Shuʿba added, from ʿAmr, from Anas: “until the Prophet ﷺ came out.”
503.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying towards a pillar.” Anas reports that the senior Companions hurried to the pillars at the Maghrib prayer. The addition “until the Prophet came out” is mentioned in the narration through Shuʿba.

504.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Juwayriya narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: “The Prophet ﷺ entered the House, and with him Usāma ibn Zayd, ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa and Bilāl; he stayed a long time, then came out. I was the first of the people to enter after him. I asked Bilāl: Where did he pray? He said: Between the two front pillars.”
504.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying between the pillars when not in congregation.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that he asked Bilāl where the Prophet had prayed in the House, and that Bilāl answered: between the two front pillars.

505.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the Kaaba, and with him Usāma ibn Zayd, Bilāl and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa al-Ḥajabī; it was locked behind him, and he stayed in it. I asked Bilāl when he came out: What did the Prophet ﷺ do? He said: He placed one pillar to his left, one pillar to his right and three pillars behind him — the House at that time stood on six pillars — then he prayed.” And Ismāʿīl said to us: Mālik narrated to me, and he said: “two pillars to his right.”
505.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying between the pillars when not in congregation.” Ibn ʿUmar relays Bilāl’s account of how the Prophet stood in relation to the pillars when he prayed in the Kaaba. At the end the text gives a differing wording through Ismāʿīl: two pillars to his right.

506.matn: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḍamra narrated to us, he said: Mūsā ibn ʿUqba narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ: “When ʿAbdallāh entered the Kaaba, he would walk straight ahead as he entered,” and he would leave the door behind his back; he walked until about three cubits remained between him and the wall in front of his face, and prayed there; he sought the place which Bilāl had told him the Prophet ﷺ prayed in. He said: And there is no blame on any of us if he prays in whichever part of the House he wishes.
506.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying between the pillars when not in congregation.” Nāfiʿ describes how ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar sought out in the Kaaba the place that Bilāl had named as the Prophet’s place of prayer. At the end the text states that it is no blame on any of them to pray in any part of the House.

507.matn: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to us, Muʿtamir narrated to us, from ʿUbaydallāh, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ: He “would set his mount crosswise and pray toward it. I said: What do you think if the mounts are stirred up? He said: He would take this saddle and set it straight, and pray toward its rear part — or he said: its back part. And Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, did it.”
507.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying towards a riding animal, a camel, a tree or a saddle.” Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet set his mount crosswise and prayed toward it; asked what about stirred-up mounts, he mentions the saddle set straight. The text notes that Ibn ʿUmar did the same.

508.matn: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “Have you made us equal to the dog and the donkey? I saw myself lying on the bed, and the Prophet ﷺ would come, stand in the middle of the bed and pray; I disliked to cross his path, so I would slip away from the foot of the bed until I had slipped out of my blanket.”
508.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying towards a bed.” ʿĀʾisha rejects equating women with the dog and the donkey and reports that she lay on the bed while the Prophet prayed in front of it, and would slip out from under the blanket so as not to cross his path.

509.matn: Abū Maʿmar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, he said: Yūnus narrated to us, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from Abū Ṣāliḥ: Abū Saʿīd said: The Prophet ﷺ said. And Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, he said: Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīra narrated to us, he said: Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl al-ʿAdawī narrated to us, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān narrated to us, he said: “I saw Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī on a Friday praying toward something that screened him from the people. A young man of the Banū Abī Muʿayṭ wanted to pass in front of him, and Abū Saʿīd pushed him in the chest. The young man looked and found no way through except in front of him; he went back to pass, and Abū Saʿīd pushed him harder than the first time. Then he reviled Abū Saʿīd, went in to Marwān and complained to him of what he had met from Abū Saʿīd. And Abū Saʿīd went in to Marwān after him. He said: What is between you and the son of your brother, Abū Saʿīd? He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: When one of you prays toward something that screens him from the people, and someone wants to pass in front of him, let him push him back; if he refuses, let him fight him, for he is a devil.”
509.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The one praying repels whoever passes in front of him.” The first chain ends with “the Prophet said” without further wording; the second chain contains the whole episode. Abū Ṣāliḥ reports how Abū Saʿīd pushed back a young man who wanted to pass in front of him, and relates the Prophet’s instruction on this before Marwān.

510.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Abū l-Naḍr, the freedman of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydallāh, from Busr ibn Saʿīd: “Zayd ibn Khālid sent him to Abū Juhaym to ask: What did he hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the one who passes in front of the one praying? Abū Juhaym said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: If the one who passes in front of the one praying knew what is upon him, it would be better for him to stand forty than to pass in front of him.” Abū l-Naḍr said: I do not know whether he said forty days, or months, or a year.
510.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The sin of passing in front of one praying.” The text gives as a warning that standing “forty” would be better than passing; the unit is uncertain, since Abū l-Naḍr does not know whether days, months or a year was said.

511.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn Khalīl narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Mushir narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim — that is, Ibn Ṣubayḥ —, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha: “What interrupts the prayer was mentioned in her presence. They said: The dog, the donkey and the woman interrupt it. She said: You have made us dogs! I saw the Prophet, peace be upon him, praying while I was between him and the qibla, lying on the bed. If I had a need, I disliked to face him, so I would slip away quietly.”
511.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man facing his companion or another while he is praying.” ʿĀʾisha objects to the statement that the dog, the donkey and the woman interrupt the prayer, and reports that she lay between the praying Prophet and the qibla and quietly slipped away when she had a need.

511.2.matn: And from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾisha: the like of it.
511.2.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places this additional chain under the chapter “A man facing his companion or another while he is praying.” It gives no wording of its own but refers with “the like of it” to the preceding hadith of ʿĀʾisha.

512.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from ʿĀʾisha, she said: “The Prophet ﷺ would pray while I slept lying across his bed; when he wanted to pray the witr, he would wake me, and I would pray the witr.”
512.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Praying behind one who is asleep.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she slept across the Prophet’s bed while he prayed, and that he woke her for the witr.

513.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Abū l-Naḍr, the freedman of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydallāh, from Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: “I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my feet in his qibla. When he prostrated, he would nudge me and I would draw in my feet; when he stood, I would stretch them out. She said: And the houses at that time had no lamps.”
513.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Voluntary prayer behind a woman.” ʿĀʾisha reports that she slept in front of the praying Prophet, drew in her feet when he prostrated and nudged her, and stretched them out again when he stood; she adds that the houses then had no lamps.

514.matn: ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Al-Aʿmash narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾisha. Al-Aʿmash said: And Muslim narrated to me, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha: “What interrupts the prayer was mentioned in her presence: the dog, the donkey and the woman. She said: You have likened us to donkeys and dogs! By Allah, I saw the Prophet ﷺ praying while I was on the bed, lying between him and the qibla. A need came over me, and I disliked to sit up and thereby disturb the Prophet ﷺ, so I slipped away from his feet.”
514.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who said nothing interrupts the prayer.” ʿĀʾisha rejects the likening of women to donkeys and dogs and reports that she lay between the praying Prophet and the qibla and slipped away when in need, so as not to disturb him.

515.matn: Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm informed us, he said: The son of Ibn Shihāb’s brother narrated to me: He asked his uncle whether anything interrupts the prayer. He said: Nothing interrupts it. ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would get up and pray at night while I lay across between him and the qibla, on the bed of his family.”
515.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who said nothing interrupts the prayer.” Asked whether anything interrupts the prayer, Ibn Shihāb answers “Nothing interrupts it” and supports this with ʿĀʾisha’s report that she lay across between the Prophet, praying at night, and the qibla.

516.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAmr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqī, from Abū Qatāda al-Anṣārī: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ “would pray while carrying Umāma, the daughter of Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — and of Abū l-ʿĀṣ ibn Rabīʿa ibn ʿAbd Shams; when he prostrated, he put her down, and when he stood, he carried her.”
516.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If one carries a little girl on his neck in prayer.” Abū Qatāda reports that the Prophet carried his granddaughter Umāma during the prayer, put her down when prostrating and carried her again when standing.

517.matn: ʿAmr ibn Zurāra narrated to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from al-Shaybānī, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād, he said: My maternal aunt Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith told me, she said: “My bed was opposite the place of prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, and sometimes his garment fell on me while I was on my bed.”
517.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If one prays towards a bed on which there is a menstruating woman.” Maymūna reports that her bed was opposite the Prophet’s place of prayer and that his garment sometimes fell on her.

518.matn: Abū l-Nuʿmān narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, he said: Al-Shaybānī — Sulaymān — narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn Shaddād narrated to us, he said: I heard Maymūna say: “The Prophet ﷺ would pray while I was asleep at his side; when he prostrated, his garment touched me while I was menstruating.” And Musaddad added, from Khālid: Sulaymān al-Shaybānī narrated to us: “while I was menstruating.”
518.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “If one prays towards a bed on which there is a menstruating woman.” Maymūna reports that she slept menstruating beside the praying Prophet and that his garment touched her when he prostrated. The addition “while I was menstruating” is also given through Musaddad.

519.matn: ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: ʿUbaydallāh narrated to us, he said: Al-Qāsim narrated to us, from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: “How evil is it that you have made us equal to the dog and the donkey! I saw myself while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying and I was lying between him and the qibla; when he wanted to prostrate, he would nudge my feet, and I would draw them in.”
519.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “May a man nudge his wife at prostration so that he can prostrate?.” ʿĀʾisha sharply rejects the equating with the dog and the donkey and reports that the Prophet nudged her feet when he wanted to prostrate and she drew them in.

520.matn: Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq al-Sūrmārī narrated to us, he said: ʿUbaydallāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbdallāh, he said: “While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing praying at the Kaaba and the gathering of Quraysh was in their sittings, one of them said: Do you not see this one who does it for show? Who among you will go to the slaughter camel of the family of so-and-so, take its stomach contents, blood and afterbirth, bring it, and let him be until he prostrates, then put it between his shoulders? The most wretched of them set off. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated, he put it between his shoulders, and the Prophet ﷺ remained in prostration. They laughed until some of them leaned on one another from laughter. Then someone went to Fāṭima, peace be upon her — she was a young girl —; she came hurrying, and the Prophet ﷺ remained in prostration until she removed it from him; then she turned to them and reviled them. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said: O Allah, seize Quraysh! O Allah, seize Quraysh! O Allah, seize Quraysh! Then he named names: O Allah, seize ʿAmr ibn Hishām, ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa, Shayba ibn Rabīʿa, al-Walīd ibn ʿUtba, Umayya ibn Khalaf, ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ and ʿUmāra ibn al-Walīd. ʿAbdallāh said: By Allah, I saw them struck down on the day of Badr; then they were dragged to the well, the well of Badr. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The people of the well have been followed by a curse.”
520.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A woman removing something harmful from one praying.” ʿAbdallāh reports how men of Quraysh placed filth between the shoulders of the praying Prophet at the Kaaba as he prostrated, and how Fāṭima removed it. The Prophet then invoked Allah against Quraysh and named seven men; ʿAbdallāh says he saw them struck down at Badr.
